subject: MSA & Order Form — allocation framework for third‑party plugin IP and indemnity
messages:
From: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@novacorp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Lee <ethan.lee@novacorp.com>, contracts@novacorp.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify indemnity allocation for plugin ecosystem (MSA + Order Form)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the redlines so far. As we work toward finalizing the MSA and order form, our legal team needs clarity on two related items that are blocking procurement: (1) allocation of responsibility when a third‑party plugin (not authored by either party) allegedly causes an IP claim; and (2) required evidence/proof that Redwood will provide in a defend scenario.

Specifically:
- If a third‑party plugin (installed by Novacorp in our environment) triggers a claim, will Redwood accept defense obligations when the alleged infringement arises from model outputs or downstream plugin behavior?
- What is the proposed evidence package and timeline (preservation, technical logs, model prompts, plugin vendor contact info)?
- Can we get a proposed cap and insurance carveout that ties to plugin provenance rather than a flat order‑form cap?

We’re trying to avoid open‑ended obligations for Novacorp procurement — happy to jump on a 30 min call to walk through concrete examples.

Best,
Maya Thompson
General Counsel, Novacorp
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@novacorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify indemnity allocation for plugin ecosystem (MSA + Order Form)

Maya —

Thanks for the clear note. Short answers up front: Redwood is prepared to defend and indemnify for third‑party IP claims that arise from our model outputs and the core service (subject to the normal MSA notice/cooperation and the Order Form caps). We believe plugin/supply‑chain exceptions are reasonable when the root cause is an independent third‑party integration that Novacorp installed and controls.

To make this concrete, we’ve drafted a technical evidence checklist and a proposed carveout language that ties defense obligations to (a) whether the plugin was certified by Redwood; (b) whether the plugin altered model prompts/weights; and (c) whether Novacorp exercised admin control to install a non‑certified plugin.

I’m attaching the latest redline (MSA_redline_kp_v3.docx) and a short plugin evidence checklist. I’ll call out items Ben and Rishi should weigh in on below.

Proposed next steps:
- Ben: confirm that the defend‑vs‑reimburse split and the suggested cap language are workable.
- Rishi: advise on what technical artifacts we can commit to provide (logs, request traces, prompt snapshots) and typical timelines for preservation.
- Maya/Ethan: if you agree in principle, we’ll prepare an Order Form exhibit that ties a lower cap to certified plugins vs a higher cap for non‑certified integrations.

Happy to take the call tomorrow at 11am PT if that works.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_redline_kp_v3.docx (Word redline), plugin-evidence-checklist.pdf (PDF checklist)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@novacorp.com>, Ethan Lee <ethan.lee@novacorp.com>, contracts@novacorp.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify indemnity allocation for plugin ecosystem (MSA + Order Form)

Kimberly / team —

I reviewed the draft language. High level thoughts:

1) Defense scope: we can accept defense for claims tied to Redwood's core model outputs and the hosted runtime. For plugin‑origin claims, propose a rebuttable presumption that Novacorp is liable when: (a) the plugin is not Redwood‑certified; (b) Novacorp installed or enabled the plugin without Redwood mediation; and (c) the plugin modifies prompts or post‑processing in a way that materially changes output.

2) Evidence package: we should commit to producing request/response traces, model prompt snapshots, and runtime logs where available within 30 days of notice (subject to preservation protocols). We should avoid committing to proprietary model internals beyond what’s necessary for triage.

3) Caps/insurance: suggest a tiered cap in the Order Form: certified plugins = standard order form cap; non‑certified plugin incidents = higher cap but with an offset for any insurance payable to Novacorp. We should also include an obligation for Novacorp to pursue remediation with the plugin vendor as part of cooperation.

I attached an exhibit spreadsheet with the proposed numeric tiers (orderform-exhibitA-proposal.xlsx).

I’ll be on the 11am PT call and can walk procurement/legal through an example scenario.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: orderform-exhibitA-proposal.xlsx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@novacorp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Lee <ethan.lee@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify indemnity allocation for plugin ecosystem (MSA + Order Form)

Maya / team —

Quick technical clarifications on what we can provide and timelines:
- Preservation: upon claim notice we will snapshot request/response logs and prompt inputs for the implicated time window; we can preserve for 90 days by default and extend on reasonable request.
- Artifacts: request/response traces, plugin metadata (version, vendor manifest), deployment config, and anonymized token‑level traces where required for forensics. We will not provide raw model weights or internal training data.
- Chain of custody: we’ll produce a signed evidence manifest for artifacts we hand over to the customer or counsel.

Operational ask for Novacorp procurement: please confirm what plugin installation controls you retain (admin console, enable/disable logs) so we can map responsibilities.

Happy to demo the evidence export on the call.

—Rishi
Principal Engineer, Infra Reliability
From: Ethan Lee <ethan.lee@novacorp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@novacorp.com>, contracts@novacorp.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify indemnity allocation for plugin ecosystem (MSA + Order Form)

Kimberly/Ben/Rishi —

Thanks for the detailed responses and the artifacts you shared on the call. Novacorp can accept a tiered cap approach but we need two confirmations before procurement will sign: (1) that Redwood will commit to the 30‑day initial evidence window and a 90‑day preservation default (as Rishi outlined); and (2) that certified plugins are clearly enumerated in the Order Form exhibit and that there is a lightweight, documented certification workflow (technical checklist + on‑boarding signoff).

If you can confirm both in writing, we’ll circulate an internal procurement approval and aim to sign the Order Form next week. Also — Maya asked us to confirm insurance interplay; we’ll accept the offset language if Redwood adds a short sentence clarifying that insurance proceeds are credited against indemnity payments.

Appreciate the practical approach — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Ethan Lee
Senior Manager, Procurement — Novacorp
